tonight.headline: Paris kicks off at 07:30 with Metcalf in the flex
body: Bad news first: at the 12:50Z snapshot DK Metcalf is still in the flex over Jalen Coker, 0.6 below the projection lineup on a coin flip, and Metcalf locks when Paris kicks off at 07:30 CDMX. After that the lineup is what it is.

Every starter you have is active or undesignated: Paris inactives are out and Warren, Metcalf and Kamara all play. ESPN has you at 62%, 130.2 to JuiceJam's 106.6. The card below is the only move, and it expires at 07:30.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: JuiceJam need Josh Jacobs — activated Saturday and expected to play (Athlon, citing Schefter) — plus Bryce Young and CeeDee Lamb to beat their numbers while Love and Jefferson miss theirs. GB-DET has the slate's biggest total, 53.5 (SI).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A late inactive among your 11:00 starters — none is designated (NFL.com report; RotoWire game pages read Sunday). Check the 09:30 CDMX inactives if you are up.

tonight.caseSources: ESPN schedule 12:50Z · Steelers.com and Yahoo inactives 25 Oct · Athlon 24 Oct · SI GB-DET

doFirst.title: Put Coker back in the flex over Metcalf
doFirst.subtitle: The projection prefers Coker 15.5 to 14.9 — a coin flip it takes. Paris inactives cleared Metcalf, so nothing unpriced moves it.

case.label: The call
case.body: lineup_check.py: lineup as set 130.3, projection lineup 130.9. The only difference is Coker over Metcalf in the flex, labelled COIN FLIP. Coin flips go to the projection with no thesis (STRATEGY §1).

case.label: What Sunday said
case.body: Metcalf, Warren and Kamara are all active for Paris (Steelers.com / Yahoo inactives, 12:05Z). Coker is undesignated and Bryce Young starts (RotoWire TB-CAR, read Sunday). Neither side has unpriced news.

case.label: Why it is a card
case.body: Metcalf went into the flex at 18:15Z Friday and is still there at the 12:50Z Sunday snapshot (activity log). If that rests on Metcalf's 15 targets in Week 6, it is volume — the backtest found it made start/sit worse at every weight. If you have a reason I cannot see, keep it: the expected cost is 0.6.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Metcalf outscores Coker in Week 7 (archive). A coin flip, so the outcome is noted, not logged as a thesis.

whatWentWrong.title: The lineup went into Paris off the projection
whatWentWrong.lead: Metcalf in the flex over Coker since 12:15 Friday — still so at 12:50Z Sunday, 0.6 below the projection lineup.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Metcalf went into the flex at 18:15Z Friday (activity log) and three briefs recommended putting Coker back. At 12:50Z Sunday it is unchanged, and Metcalf locks at 07:30 CDMX.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: Small here — a coin flip worth 0.6 — but it is the same pattern that cost weeks 1-2: moving off the projection on last week's volume (Metcalf's 15 targets in Week 6). The rule is the projection unless news it has not priced.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Metcalf outscores Coker in Week 7 (archive) — then the move cost nothing this week, though the rule stands. Graded on outcome, no thesis.

whatWentWrong.title: Week 6 was won with 11.0 left on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: Kamara's 14.9 sat behind Allgeier's 5.8 and Love's 20.2 behind Allen's 18.3 — both projection calls, neither an override.

case.label: The numbers
case.body: 122.6 to 82.94 over Bok-aneers; best possible lineup 133.6 (week-6 archive, recomputed this run).

case.label: The lesson
case.body: Both were projection calls that lost. The fix is not to override — it is to set the lineup every week, which is done for Week 7: the lineup as set is the projection lineup.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: A Week 7 lineup set by projection leaves more than 15 points on the bench (archive).

worthALook.lead: Week 8 tight-end cover — weaker now that Bowers practised in full on Friday.

case.label: The cost

case.label: When to act
case.body: Next Tuesday on Week 8 projections, dropping a bye-week body. Changes if he draws under 5 targets against the Rams with Bowers active.

doNotChase.name: Tyler Allgeier
doNotChase.lead: Jeremiyah Love is ruled out again — and it is still a committee Bam Knight won last week.

case.label: The case for
case.body: Love OUT for Week 7 (ankle), Arizona resting him until he is 100% (SI 22 Oct; NFL.com Week 7 report). Allgeier took 56% of snaps and 18 carries in Week 6 and should get the goal line against a Denver defence 7th-most generous to backs (SI 22 Oct; DeepMetric).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 18 carries for 38 yards, 2.1 a carry, against Bam Knight's 15 for 80 on 44% of snaps (SI 22 Oct). SI's own read: a bigger committee than expected, no clear split.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Love placed on IR and Allgeier named the lead — and even then not a reversal of the 21 Oct drop.

doNotChase.sources: SI 22 Oct · NFL.com Week 7 report · DeepMetric

doNotChase.name: Bam Knight
doNotChase.lead: Out-gained Allgeier 80 to 38 — and is still the second back in a split.

case.label: The case for
case.body: 15 carries for 80 yards (5.3 a carry), 2 catches on 44% of snaps in Week 6 with Love out; SI calls him a viable flex with Love out again (SI 22 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 44% of snaps, behind Allgeier's 56% and the goal line; a free agent filling a vacancy that ends when Love returns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Knight out-snaps Allgeier at Denver and Love goes to IR.

doNotChase.name: Roschon Johnson
doNotChase.lead: This week's riser has stopped rising — 2 carries on Thursday; D'Andre Swift took the backfield.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Swift played 86% of snaps and handled 26 of 28 running-back opportunities; Johnson 14% of snaps, 2 carries for 13 (RotoWire usage 22 Oct). The ownership jump was bought on Monangai's injury, and Swift, not Johnson, inherited it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Swift hurt and Monangai (turf toe, uncertain for Week 8 at Seattle per RotoWire) still out — then Johnson is the only back left. Carried from Friday's research (RotoWire TNF usage 22 Oct); this run found nothing newer.
